title: Dual of the Koszul resolution of a regular quotient
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and let f_1,\ldots,f_r be a finite Koszul-regular sequence in A [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Put I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r), B=A/I, C=I/I^2, and N=\operatorname{Hom}_B(C,B). Let K_A(f_\bullet) be the Koszul complex, regarded as a bounded complex of finite free A-modules resolving B. Then the total Hom complex \operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(K_A(f_\bullet),A) is canonically quasi-isomorphic in D(A) to the A-complex obtained from the B-complex \bigwedge_B^r N[-r] by restriction of scalars along A\to B. In particular H^i(\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(K_A(f_\bullet),A))=0 for i\neq r and H^r\cong\bigwedge_B^r N as B-modules. The quasi-isomorphism is functorial under localization of A, compatible with the induced B-module structure on the target, and the induced isomorphism \operatorname{Ext}^r_A(B,A)\cong\bigwedge_B^r N depends only on the ideal I, not on the choice of the Koszul-regular generating sequence f_1,\ldots,f_r.

proof.text: Write E=A^{\oplus r} with basis e_1,\ldots,e_r and let phi:E\to A send e_i to f_i. By the definition of the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], K_j=\bigwedge_A^jE, K_j=0 for j>r, and every K_j is finite free. The augmentation K_0=A\to B is a quasi-isomorphism because Koszul-regularity says H_j(K)=0 for j\ne0 and d_1(E)=I [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence, def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex].

For each j, the determinant pairing identifies Hom_A(\bigwedge^jE,A) with the corresponding complementary exterior-power dual, using the canonical exterior pairing [lem-sc-exterior-power-dual-pairing]. In the basis e_i this is the map sending a dual wedge and a primal wedge to the determinant of their evaluation matrix. Dualizing the Koszul differential therefore gives the cochain differential obtained by wedging with the covector phi; this equality follows by evaluating both maps on basis wedges and using the alternating determinant formula.

Write δ_j for the degree-one dual derivation sending e_i to the Kronecker delta δ_{ij}. Under the determinant pairing of Step 2, Hom_A^i(K,A) is identified with the span of δ_{j_1}\cdotsδ_{j_i}. Directly from d(e_i)=f_i and the Koszul sign rule, its cochain differential is multiplication by -\sum_j f_jδ_j. Evaluation on the top wedge e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r therefore gives an isomorphism of graded A-modules Hom_A^\bullet(K,A)\cong K_A(f_\bullet)[-r], which, with the sign conventions of Tag 0BQZ (total Hom differential as in Stacks, and d_{K[n]}=(-1)^nd_K), commutes with differentials when r is odd and anticommutes with them when r is even (for r=1 both complexes are A\xrightarrow{-f_1}A in degrees 0,1 and the map is the identity); in the anticommuting case composing with (-1)^n in degree n gives an isomorphism of complexes, so in all cases Hom_A^\bullet(K,A)\cong K_A(f_\bullet)[-r] as complexes. Since K has homology B in degree 0 and no other homology by Koszul-regularity, the dual complex has cohomology only in degree r. The degree-r determinant classes identify with the dual conormal module N=Hom_B(I/I^2,B), and their alternating products give H^r\cong\bigwedge_B^rN. The same formulas are preserved after localizing A at any g.

The determinant classes just used are intrinsic: the map from the top exterior power of the dual conormal module to Ext^r_A(B,A) sends a local dual basis to the corresponding determinant class, and the determinant change-of-basis formula shows that it is unchanged when a different Koszul-regular generating sequence of I is chosen. The same determinant formula commutes with localization, so these local identifications glue and depend only on I. Hence the total Hom complex is canonically quasi-isomorphic in D(A) to the restriction of scalars of\n\bigwedge_B^rN[-r].

For the cohomology clause, use the normalized comparison-existence clause and the conormal basis [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis]. The exterior pairing is injective: the exterior powers of the dual basis have dual coordinate evaluations by the determinant formula [lem-sc-exterior-power-dual-pairing]. Conormal vectors are surjective because f generates I. Hence two normalized comparisons agree on every conormal wedge, thus on their top components; all other components have zero target. The given comparison is therefore a quasi-isomorphism. Extension by zero preserves quasi-isomorphisms; applying Q makes an isomorphism. Homology of the single complex gives the vanishing and the top-degree isomorphism. Choose M to be the actual determinant module and e the identity, with iota inverse to the homology map. Naturality of homology projection gives the required equation on cycles.

For change of generators, the equality g composed with t = f implies c_g composed with t = c_f. Apply the injective cotangent-to-quotient-square map and evaluate finite linear combinations to prove this equality. Lift each conormal vector through the surjective c_f. The normalization formula for phi evaluated on those lifts equals the formula for psi evaluated on their t-images, since exteriorPower.map sends a decomposable wedge to the wedge of its images. Injectivity of the exterior-dual pairing, obtained from the conormal basis, gives equality of comparison values. This proof does not need regularity of g.

For the quotient augmentation, identify the zeroth Koszul boundary under exteriorPower.zeroEquiv and exteriorPower.oneEquiv with Finsupp.linearCombination A f. Its image is I because f generates I. Compose the degree-zero equivalence with I.mkQ to construct q, and use ChainComplex.toSingle₀Equiv to construct the chain augmentation. The short complex d₁, q is exact and q is surjective, hence q is a cokernel of d₁. Uniqueness of cokernels makes the induced map on opcycles an isomorphism; ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_isIso_descOpcycles proves the degree-zero quasi-isomorphism. In positive degrees use Koszul-regularity and the exactness of the single complex. Extend the augmentation along embeddingDownNat and compose with extendSingleIso. Both operations preserve quasi-isomorphisms; their degree-zero formulas give precisely the quotient evaluation equation. This also covers r=0 and I=top without nontriviality assumptions.

For exists_unique_koszul_conormal_comparison, take the normalized quasi-isomorphism from lem-sc-koszul-conormal-comparison-existence. Obtain the conormal basis from lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis. Two normalized comparisons agree after pairing with each decomposable conormal wedge: lift every conormal vector through the surjective generator map and use the identical normalization equations. The exterior dual pairing is injective by dual-basis coordinates. Thus the top components agree; to_single_hom_ext identifies the complex maps. This closes only uniqueness, leaving existence as the strictly smaller split theorem.

For localization, obtain Koszul regularity by flat base change. Construct the span equality using Ideal.map_span and the quotient map using Ideal.quotientMap. Obtain the two coefficient maps and their evaluation equations. Evaluate the required comparison square on each wedge of the localized conormal basis. Each such wedge lifts through an original standard-basis wedge. The two normalization equations and the coefficient-map equations agree because the quotient ring map preserves multiplication, powers, -1 and quotient images. Injectivity of the exterior dual pairing proves the square.

For the intrinsic Ext determinant clause use the repaired existential roof-normalization theorem to select e. Do not apply a universal normalization statement to an arbitrary quotient-linear equivalence. Derive quotient-linearity for this very e by lifting quotient scalars to A and applying the Ext scalar-composition equations and e.map_smul.
